PullRequest.Title: Sessions: shared fixes for hosting sessions UI outside the Agents window
PullRequest.Body:

**Merge order**: before #348308, which builds on it, and the rest of the stack (#348309, the features).

Shared fixes in the sessions code that the Agents window and other hosts of its sessions UI both use. Each one is valid on its own; none changes what the Agents window shows with AI features enabled.

## Changes

- **Null chat window service.** The phone's `MobileNullChatWindowService` moves to `vs/workbench/contrib/chatWindow/browser/nullChatWindowService.ts` as `NullChatWindowService` (with a generic message), so any window without separate chat windows can provide `IChatWindowService`, which the session chat's input toolbar injects.
- **Session attention service registration.** `ISessionAttentionService` is registered once, in its own module, rather than by the Agents window's contribution: every window that loads it gets it, and none registers it twice.
- **AI features disabled.** The new-session composer toolbar, the model picker, the agent host agent and session config pickers, and the agent picker keybinding are hidden while `ChatContextKeys.enabled` is false.
- **Sessions outside a provider's listing scope.** Reopening a closed item and resolving a session's settings file look sessions up with `getSession(resource)` and `getAllSessions()`, so they also find sessions of other folders that a scoped provider does not list.
- **Stale translation resource.** `vs/sessions/contrib/chatEditor` is removed from `build/lib/i18n.resources.json`: its folder moved to `vs/workbench` in #347696.

## How to test

1. With `chat.disableAIFeatures` on, open the Agents window: the composer toolbar and the agent host pickers do not show.
2. In the Agents window, close a session's chat, scope the list to another folder, and run Reopen Closed: the chat reopens.
3. The Agents window and the phone layout behave as before otherwise.

Scenarios.Scenario: Loading sessions UI in desktop/editor/mobile windows and registering the null chat-window and attention services
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation registers service descriptors; both services remain delayed, so neither NullChatWindowService nor SessionAttentionService construction is added to startup's critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One registration per window/module load; no collection-sized work was added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous work or queue is started by the changed registration/import lines.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read. Delayed singleton instantiation remains demand-driven before and after the change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the changed singleton declarations use InstantiationType.Delayed, and the same sessions contribution that previously registered the attention service now imports its self-registering module.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: the changed work is descriptor registration and import relocation only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Registration ownership moved without eager construction, I/O, IPC, or repeated startup work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Showing and updating the Sessions Inbox attention view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionAttentionService is constructed when injected, but tracking activates only while an Inbox consumer holds acquireSessionAttention(); GitHub refreshes and chat-model loads are launched in the background rather than awaited by rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh and poll pull-request, review-thread, and CI models for distinct referenced pull requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per distinct referenced pull request while Inbox attention tracking is demanded; model identities suppress duplicate refreshes and model references share polling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SessionAttentionService implementation and demand gate performed these operations before the registration was moved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background work is not awaited by Inbox rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or load a chat model for a NeedsInput chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight load per active NeedsInput chat resource; loaded and in-flight maps coalesce repeats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical demand-driven loading existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Launched asynchronously and not awaited by the reactive attention calculation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct active session pull-request references and NeedsInput chats, but only while the Inbox grouping is visible.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Potential background work is per distinct pull request/chat, with chat loads coalesced per resource; the diff does not change concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHub model references and refreshed identities are reused; loaded/in-flight chat maps provide positive and in-flight caching and are cleaned when resources leave demand.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; only singleton registration location changed, while constructor, demand gate, deduplication, and cleanup are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External provider latency varies, but no changed line increases call count, scheduling, or lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Existing background network/IPC behavior is neither introduced nor amplified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reopening the most recently closed session or chat in a scoped editor window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command synchronously resolves the recorded resource through getSession, then an existing chat reopen may await provider resource resolution and session/chat loading. The changed lookup itself is an in-memory traversal and is not awaited on a remote listing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cold agent-host session catalog refresh via connection.listSessions().
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one current refresh per agent-host provider, with calls coalesced and one optional trailing refresh; provider subscription already requests the unscoped catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider registration already called getAllSessions, and unscoped getSessions also called getAllSessions; the changed command does not add another uncoalesced round trip.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: getAllSessions may schedule it when cold but does not await it, so the reopen lookup proceeds from the current cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a session resource through registered providers and load/prepare the selected session/chat if needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Providers are consulted serially until one resolves the resource; one selected chat/session is then opened.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: ClosedItemHistory invoked the same openChat callback after its old listed-session lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This existing open path may block completion of reopening.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered providers and total cached sessions; history cardinality is fixed at one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resource resolution is serialized across providers; agent-host catalog refreshes are coalesced per provider; only one closed history item is retained and reopened.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm lookups enumerate cached arrays. On a cold agent-host cache, refresh is shared and not awaited; there is no new retry or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; getSession traverses all provider caches and the downstream open path is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Total session history can vary, but the new all-session traversal is linear, synchronous, and only occurs on the explicit reopen command.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The broader lookup enables hidden sessions, adds no uncoalesced boundary call, and runs once per explicit reopen.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, editing, and cleaning up an agent-session settings document for a session outside listing scope
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A synthetic filesystem read serializes current config and performs an in-memory all-session lookup before registering a JSON schema. Saving parses the document and uses the existing replaceSessionConfig operation. Provider removal performs synchronous schema cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cold agent-host session catalog refresh via connection.listSessions().
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced refresh per provider; normal provider registration has already requested this catalog before the AfterRestored settings contribution is used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider catalog was already initialized through management-service provider subscription and through unscoped getSessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous getAllSessions call can schedule but does not await refresh; readFile uses the currently cached config/session state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace one session's configuration on save.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One replace operation per explicit file save.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The write path and replace call are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by writeFile and therefore on the save critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All cached sessions known by the selected provider rather than only the scoped listed subset. Config-change lookup and provider-removal cleanup are O(total cached sessions).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reads and schema updates are synchronous per event; catalog refresh is coalesced per provider; saves issue one awaited replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session data is cache-backed; schema registration is lazy on first read and skips refresh when schema identity is unchanged. Provider cleanup disposes only registered schema map entries even though it enumerates all known sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the broader linear traversal and high that no new awaited boundary is added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A provider may retain more hidden sessions than the scoped list, but the added cost is an array construction/search on explicit read or config-change events and a one-time provider-removal traversal; no evidence establishes a realistic user-visible delay.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff broadens local cleanup/lookup cardinality to preserve hidden-session schemas, but does not add per-session I/O, IPC, eager schema registration, or an unbounded retained collection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering composer/model/agent controls when AI features are enabled or disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Menu visibility recomputation evaluates added context-key expressions before creating action view items; when disabled, the controls are suppressed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed set of toolbar/menu actions, independent of session history or row count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous menu expression evaluation only; no queue, listener fan-out, or asynchronous work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Context-key/menu infrastructure remains unchanged; no cache keys or invalidation behavior are added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; all changed production lines in these pickers/toolbars add ChatContextKeys.enabled predicates only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the added predicates are constant-size boolean expressions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The change reduces disabled-state rendering and does not add scalable UI work or expensive boundaries.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 22 changed files and all diff pages. Traced startup registration, Inbox demand, explicit reopen, synthetic settings read/write/cleanup, menu rendering, provider caches, and transitive IPC/network paths. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
